diagrams.title: The Sub-$1,000 Launch Sequence
diagrams.subtitle: Spend on the phone first, buy insurance and supplies only when a deal closes
diagrams.caption: AJ Simmons sequences a lean launch around a $99 CBN membership, a $200 LLC budget, a $25 domain and 400 cold calls in week one, deferring insurance and supplies until a contract is ready to close.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Step order follows AJ Simmons's launch plan and operator gates. Dollar figures and call counts are his attributed claims; funnel yields are his ranges, not guarantees.
diagrams.note: Source AJ SIMMONS (VrlDbQP4iQI at 00:14:20, 00:15:12, 00:16:03; QBuGc_Q36dg at 00:05:39; mk-8avM72Ms at 00:02:52).

stages.label: Lean launch kit
stages.detail: $99 CBN membership, $200 LLC budget and a $25 domain; no supplies bought yet.

stages.label: 400 calls in week one
stages.detail: Call 100 businesses Monday through Friday; 400 calls yield 1-4 walkthroughs.

stages.label: Measure cleanable footage
stages.detail: Laser-measure only cleanable square footage; bidding the whole building sends the price too high.

stages.label: Proposal within 2-3 hours
stages.detail: Slow turnaround turns the walkthrough into wasted time.

stages.label: Close, then insure and stock
stages.detail: Buy the quoted policy and supplies at close; push upfront payment, otherwise net 10 or net 15.

diagrams.title: Big-Account Math, From Portfolio to Porter Bill Rate
diagrams.subtitle: Five $5k accounts down to the $26 hour that prices a day porter
diagrams.caption: Five $5k accounts equal $300,000 a year, and a 4-hour labor-only day porter prices at $2,262 a month on 87 billable hours at a $26 bill rate.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Values mix units by design and narrow from annual portfolio revenue to a single bill-rate hour. Every figure is stated by the practitioners; none is modeled.
diagrams.note: Sources The Janitorial Store (1c9Ty46MQbg at 00:01:28) for porter pricing; Big Accounts chapter summary for the five $5k accounts figure; OctoClean Media (52I2LNERY3E at 00:20:41) for the wage-plus-load gate.

stages.label: Five $5k office accounts
stages.detail: Five accounts at $5,000 a month each.

stages.label: One $5k office account
stages.detail: Large accounts carry 35-40% gross margin versus about 50-60% on small ones.

stages.label: 4-hour day porter price
stages.detail: Labor-only porter, 4 hours a day, 5 days, 10am-2pm.

stages.label: Porter billable hours
stages.conversion: 1,040 hrs a year divided by 12, rounded
stages.detail: A day porter can handle a zone of about 30 to 40 bathroom fixtures.

stages.label: Porter bill rate
stages.conversion: $18 wage loaded with taxes and profit
stages.detail: Bidding $16 on a $15 wage loses money on every hour.

diagrams.title: 100 Cold Calls Down to 2 Walkthroughs
diagrams.subtitle: Cold calling opens a door rather than closing a deal
diagrams.caption: Carolyn Arellano's funnel turns 100 calls into 20-30 reached, 10-15 conversations, 3-5 qualified and 1-2 walkthroughs; 8 walkthroughs a month at a 25% close rate equal 2 contracts a month.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Bars use the upper end of each stated range (30 reached, 15 conversations, 5 qualified, 2 walkthroughs). Deductions are the gaps between those stated stages.

diagrams.title: The Percentages Behind the First Contract
diagrams.subtitle: Won on dependability and margin discipline, not the lowest bid
diagrams.caption: Roughly 90% of commercial prospects already have a cleaner; refusing to be the cheapest bid lifted one closing rate from 10% to 25-35%, while margin floors sit at 30% with about 25% for strategic accounts.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Where a practitioner gave a range without a typical value, typical is the midpoint of that range. Single-point claims use the same figure for min, max and typical.
diagrams.note: Sources Cleaning Launch (V84a_KWRYU4 at 00:01:22); ONLY MAIDS PODCAST with Joseph D Adams (aQj7G__L-iE at 00:07:34 and 00:08:41); OctoClean Media (1tf8JMWxi98 at 00:00:44).

diagrams.title: Four Gates Before a Bid Leaves the Building
diagrams.subtitle: Scope, labor, full cost, target margin, then a stress test
diagrams.caption: Worked bids convert footage and fixture counts into hours, load the wage, divide by one minus the margin, multiply by 4.33 weeks, and survive one extra worker hour per visit.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate thresholds are the practitioners' own figures; the 25% to about 13.4% collapse comes from a 20,000 sq ft, three-visit-a-week model priced at $2,800.
diagrams.note: Sources Commercial Cleaning CEO (IMbK5m7qbY0 at 00:04:42, 00:07:02, 00:10:01); Channel Zero Marketing (Ey7iPjW1uZQ at 00:13:44); Bid & Profit Lab (T-l3Df3Iino at 00:04:10 and 00:04:26).

nodes.question: Is measured footage cut 10-20% for walls and fixed furniture, with toilets and urinals counted as units?
nodes.fail_action: Remeasure and recount fixtures; bathroom counts hide one stall or twenty.

nodes.question: Is the wage loaded with payroll liabilities, such as a $15 cleaner costing $17.71 an hour?
nodes.fail_action: Stack unemployment, FICA and workers comp onto the base wage before pricing.

nodes.question: Is price set as cost divided by one minus margin, billed on 4.33 weeks a month?
nodes.fail_action: Reprice; using 4 weeks on a $65 twice-weekly visit gives away about $516 a year.

nodes.question: Does margin hold with one extra worker hour per visit?
nodes.fail_action: Rescope or reprice; one extra hour cut a 25% margin to about 13.4%.

diagrams.title: Classification and Coverage Around the Owner
diagrams.subtitle: Decided by control, not by the label or the form
diagrams.caption: Operators, accountants and insurance agents converge on control as the test for W2 versus 1099, and price bonds, general liability and workers comp before bidding.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Premiums and rates are quotes reported at the time of filming; New York comp rates are 2022 base rates for class codes 9026, 9027 and 9028.
diagrams.note: Sources Commercial Cleaning CEO (9BXhBVRp_XU at 00:03:59); Surety Bonds Direct (uMW_ZJMW0ZU at 00:04:12); The Janitorial Store (YC2NrvVJqlg at 00:03:13); The Professional Cleaner (DDLzG49aDvU at 00:03:20); The Coyle Group (HSh0vcHYmUI at 00:00:56).

diagrams.title: Where Each Account Dollar Goes
diagrams.subtitle: Labor-hour pricing with a 40/30/30 split and supplies billed on top
diagrams.total_range: 100% of base billing (40/30/30), plus a 3-5% supply charge
diagrams.caption: Rudy Perez aims every account at 40% labor, 30% other expenses and 30% profit; Carolyn Arellano bills 3% of the base rate for supplies on top of the labor figure.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The 40/30/30 split is a per-account target, not an industry average. The supply band spans Carolyn Arellano's 3% and the 3-5% range cited across bidders.
diagrams.note: Sources 7 Figure Cleaning with Rudy Perez (1_z-Kgj0GYM at 00:01:17); Carolyn Arellano (IJlyq2UAXqU at 00:06:05); AJ SIMMONS (7VHAkhs_HG4 at 00:02:48).

buckets.label: Labor
buckets.notes: AJ Simmons bills double the cleaner wage, $15 paid becoming $30 billed.

buckets.label: Supplies, insurance, taxes, CPA
buckets.notes: Load back office, transportation, churn and overtime before the account goes out.

buckets.label: Profit
buckets.notes: Rudy Perez's worked example uses a $40 hourly charge.

buckets.label: Supply charge on top of base
buckets.notes: 3% of a $2,166.66 base is $64.98 a month (Carolyn Arellano).

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Buying a Cleaning Franchise
diagrams.subtitle: The contract, not the mop, is the business
diagrams.caption: Ex-franchisees and a franchisor founder describe fees stacking to 20-35% of billing, sometimes 40%, finder fees at 4x monthly value, and real pay near $7 an hour.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week ordering is an editorial sequence of the testified checks; no practitioner set durations for them.
diagrams.note: Sources Mike Mak (6MDrTK46_8g at 00:04:31 and 00:06:32); Commercial Cleaning CEO (xqw9zag57Uk at 00:05:18); Clean For A Dream (fs86ZhCBfJ8 at 00:30:23 and 00:56:29); AJ SIMMONS (Bbay8f0-XFM at 00:03:28).

weeks.title: Interrogate the fee stack
weeks.deliverable: Written answers on support fees and what each new account costs
weeks.gate: Royalty near 10%, marketing 2-10% and admin 5-10% totaled against 20-35% drag

weeks.title: Check reputation
weeks.deliverable: Complaint search, Ripoff Report check, tenured and exited franchisee interviews
weeks.gate: Buying in is like getting married; unresolved complaints stop the deal

weeks.title: Convert the package into hours
weeks.deliverable: Post-fee payout divided by $16-$30 an hour versus about 100 hours worked
weeks.gate: A $705 payout on about 100 hours is roughly $7 an hour

weeks.title: Confirm contract ownership
weeks.deliverable: Answer on whether the franchise can reassign happy accounts
weeks.gate: If accounts can be reassigned, walk away from a glorified-employee role
